criteria_results.text: A role-scoped local Ollama session can invoke OpenCode-native tools, including skill, while MCP tools remain limited to the profile's allowed MCP servers.
criteria_results.notes: Manual screenshot showed two `Tool "skill" is not permitted for this agent's role and was blocked.` errors in a Secretary session scoped to rhythm and obsidian. The embedded OpenCode session had actually completed the daily-morning-briefing skill call, proving the API stream bridge was falsely applying the MCP server allowlist to OpenCode's native skill tool. A bridge regression test now covers skill, task, read, and bash while retaining denial of a non-Rhythm MCP tool.

issues.description: The local-provider integration proceeded without an acceptance contract covering role-scoped native-tool dispatch, so the MCP/native-tool boundary was absent from automated verification.
issues.detected_by: Conversation tool-call review and absence of a local-Ollama contract under docs/ai/contracts.

issues.description: The failure-postmortem completion checklist was not expanded into explicit TodoWrite items at skill entry.

failure_output: Error: Tool "skill" is not permitted for this agent's role and was blocked.
suggested_follow_up: Every role-scoping contract should separately assert OpenCode-native permission behavior and MCP-server dispatch behavior so the two capability boundaries cannot be conflated.
